request.system: You are a senior clinical coder in an Australian public hospital with fifteen years of experience coding inpatient episodes in ICD-10-AM. You are careful, conservative, and you never invent a code you are not sure of the chapter for.

messages.content:
Code the episode of care below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed. Give the three-character ICD-10-AM category for the principal diagnosis.

Hospital course:
Hospital Course:
Admission Date: [DATE]
Discharge Date: [DATE]
Length of Stay: [NUMBER] days

Patient Information:
Name: [NAME]
Age: 76 years old
Gender: Male
Admission Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course Summary:
The patient, a 76-year-old Caucasian male with a family history of Parkinson's disease, was admitted to our hospital after experiencing a shuffling gait. Neurological examination revealed bilateral rigidity and slow gait with reduced arm swing, as well as processing speed and memory difficulties. The patient also presented with urinary retention, orthostatic hypotension, erectile dysfunction, and stridor. Carbidopa/levodopa was unsuccessfully administered. The patient was diagnosed with multiple system atrophy (MSA), due to levodopa-unresponsive parkinsonism and autonomic dysfunction.

During the hospital course, the patient received comprehensive care from a multidisciplinary team, including neurologists and primary care physicians. Management of orthostatic hypotension and urinary retention were coordinated with the urology department. The patient was administered supportive therapy, including physical therapy and occupational therapy, to address mobility and activities of daily living. The patient's condition remained stable throughout his hospital stay.

At the time of discharge, the patient was instructed to continue with his current medications and follow up with his primary care physician and neurologist. The patient was also instructed to contact his healthcare provider if any new or worsening symptoms arise.
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Follow-up Instructions:
1. Continue current medication regimen as prescribed.
2. Follow up with primary care physician and neurologist.
3. Contact healthcare provider if any new or worsening symptoms arise.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
**CODE: G23**

The condition chiefly responsible for this admission is **multiple system atrophy (MSA)**. It was established after investigation, when the patient's parkinsonism did not respond to carbidopa/levodopa and he also had autonomic dysfunction.

- **What is not principal:** The shuffling gait, rigidity, urinary retention, orthostatic hypotension, erectile dysfunction and stridor are all manifestations of MSA. None of them should be sequenced as the principal diagnosis.
- **Subtype:** Parkinsonism is the dominant presenting feature, so this reads as the parkinsonian type (MSA-P). In WHO ICD-10 that is G23.2 (category G23, other degenerative diseases of basal ganglia).
- **Uncertainty:** I have not confirmed that the ICD-10-AM edition in use carries the MSA-P inclusion at G23.2. Please check the Alphabetic Index for your edition before finalising.
  - Older editions index MSA, or MSA with autonomic failure (Shy-Drager), to G90.3 (multi-system degeneration of the autonomic nervous system).
  - If the documentation or your edition supports that, the category would be **G90**.
